faq.title: What this experience proves.
faq.description: The dogfood is a consumer of Identity, not a new authority over it.

items.question: Is LaunchKit the Identity design system?
items.answer: No. LaunchKit is a replaceable presentation adapter. It consumes reviewed Identity outputs and owns only landing composition.

items.question: Does Zensical own the documentation source?
items.answer: No. Repository-owned Markdown is durable source. Zensical is pinned rendering and navigation infrastructure for the docs subtree.

items.question: Can this page change canonical tokens or assets?
items.answer: No. The build is read-only over reviewed Identity outputs and fails when selected bytes, alt text, provenance, approval, or release evidence drift.

items.question: How does rollback work?
items.answer: The organization route owner re-promotes a preceding verified composite. The canonical Brand Kit rolls back independently through an earlier stable annotated Identity tag.

documentation.title: Identity documentation
documentation.introduction: Use Identity by selecting reviewed outputs, verifying their release evidence, and keeping framework adapters downstream from canonical brand intent.

pages.title: Start with Identity
pages.summary: Choose the smallest reviewed projection your surface needs.
pages.body:
Identity separates canonical intent from its replaceable projections. Begin with the repository contracts and generated `assets/identity/manifest.json`, select a stable release, then record its tag, commit, source digest, and relevant package checksum in the consuming surface. Never copy token values, mascot facts, rights, provenance, or approvals into framework configuration.

The canonical public Brand Kit remains at [identity.egohygiene.io](https://identity.egohygiene.io/). This product experience is a dogfooded consumer of those same reviewed outputs.

pages.title: Intent to projection
pages.summary: Trace every public artifact back to reviewed intent and evidence.
pages.body:
The compiler validates repository input, resolves inheritance and aliases, plans exact mutations, renders offline, and verifies the resulting bytes. Generated projections remain reproducible because source paths, release identity, checksums, and approvals stay attached to the handoff.

LaunchKit and Zensical consume those outputs read-only. They own presentation and navigation, not brand truth. A framework change therefore requires a reviewed adapter-pin update and fresh deterministic, accessibility, route, and visual evidence.

pages.title: Kern
pages.summary: Use Identity's approved guide with his governed description, rights, and provenance.
pages.body:
Kern is Identity's hooded guide: three warm-white glowing eyes and a luminous diamond kernel integrated into charcoal and violet robes. Approved full, portrait, and icon projections contain no floating objects, orbiting rings, or particle effects.

Kern is licensed under CC BY 4.0. Use the exact alternative text, asset checksum, approval evidence, provenance, and guidance resolved from `assets/identity/mascot/manifest.json` and the canonical mascot package. He may support a story but must never be the sole carrier of meaning.

pages.title: Release evidence
pages.summary: Verify the release, inputs, exact bytes, and rollback target before installation.
pages.body:
`/identity/publication.json` binds the candidate release tag and full commit to a source digest, framework pins, mascot projection, evidence references, complete file inventory, and artifact digest. `SHA256SUMS` verifies every non-recursive artifact member.

The route owner installs the reviewed archive without rebuilding it, compares the binding with `https://identity.egohygiene.io/site.json`, checks the canonical HTTPS routes, and retains the preceding verified composite for rollback. A candidate build is review evidence only until its stable annotated release exists.

architecture.title: Identity publication architecture
architecture.introduction: Canonical Identity outputs feed replaceable landing and documentation profiles; one bounded composer emits an immutable handoff for the organization route owner.
architecture.diagram:
flowchart TD
  intent[Reviewed Identity intent] --> compiled[Compiled Identity outputs]
  compiled --> landing[LaunchKit landing]
  compiled --> docs[Zensical surfaces]
  landing --> artifact[Content-addressed composite]

decisions.title: Keep authoring and generated outputs separate
decisions.summary: Human-authored intent remains distinguishable from deterministic projections and transient review evidence.

legal.title: Identity legal and trust
legal.introduction: Rights, accessibility, provenance, and artifact boundaries remain visible alongside the product experience.

pages.title: Licensing and attribution
pages.summary: Separate repository code terms from governed asset rights.
pages.body:
Identity repository code and documentation are governed by the licenses published in the source repository. Individual asset packages may carry different rights. Kern is published under CC BY 4.0 and requires attribution as described by the mascot package.

Before redistribution, inspect the selected release's manifest, rights reference, provenance, and approval evidence. Do not infer rights from a preview image or from this explanatory page.

pages.title: Accessibility
pages.summary: The experience treats semantic content and governed alternative text as release gates.
pages.body:
The composite is checked for keyboard navigation, visible focus, semantic headings and landmarks, alternative text, responsive layouts, reduced motion, high contrast, no-JavaScript readability, and serious or critical automated accessibility violations across major browser engines.

Report a barrier through the Identity issue tracker with the affected route, browser, assistive technology, and steps to reproduce. Automated checks support but do not replace human review.

pages.title: Publication and privacy boundary
pages.summary: Identity hands off static reviewed bytes and does not control the organization host.
pages.body:
This repository emits a static, content-addressed `/identity/` composite. It does not own the `egohygiene.io` homepage, DNS, TLS, hosting configuration, or organization-wide privacy policy. Relay and the organization route owner install exact reviewed bytes and verify the live release binding.

The repository-owned artifact does not add analytics, advertising, account forms, or runtime mutation. Host-level services and policies remain the responsibility of the organization route owner and must be reviewed independently.
